_note: Everywhere either surface keeps something, and whether it hangs under the account (so it must be on the server and reach every device) or belongs to this device. Hidde, 2026-09-11: "alles moet cross device beschikbaar zijn wat onder je account hangt. Check of dit voor alles geldt." Checked by scripts/crossdevice.py, which refuses a store nobody has ruled on; it cannot tell whether the verdict is right.

recent_searches.why: Recent searches under the empty search field, app (Kit/RecentSearches.swift, inside MapSearch) and web (search-form.ts): what a signed-in person picked, at most five within 90 days. Table recent_searches (supabase/recent-searches.sql), read and written straight from the server; on the device only in the open screen's memory, never in UserDefaults or localStorage, so no key is written and `keep` holds this entry.
recent_searches.off: Nothing, because nothing is written to the device: signed out, neither surface asks for the rows or records a pick, and the screen's in-memory copy goes with the screen. Deleting the account removes the rows by the foreign key's on delete cascade.

saved.entries.v1.why: Hearts and ticks. Tables saves and visited, merged as a union by CloudSync on launch and on sign-in; the website reads the same two tables.
saved.entries.v1.off: Saved.forgetLocally(), called by ContentView.forgetIfSignedOut() at launch. It empties this phone only; the saves and visited tables keep the collection.

file:Sightings.swift.why: The trees you added and every photograph you took, including one taken while ticking off a tree of ours. Table sightings plus the private sightings bucket, pushed by SightingSync on every change and on launch. FILE STORE rather than UserDefaults: Documents/sightings, found by the file-store scan.
file:Sightings.swift.off: Sightings.forgetLocally(), called by ContentView.forgetIfSignedOut(); only the ones the account already holds, so nothing unsent is thrown away.

blocked-accounts.why: Who you have blocked. Table blocks; the local copy is an echo so a block holds with no network, and the server is the truth on a second phone.
blocked-accounts.off: Nothing, deliberately: a signed-out phone shows no people to block or unblock, and a block is a safety decision that should not lapse when a session expires. The blocks table is the truth and the next sign-in reloads it.

distanceUnit.why: Kilometres or miles. Column units on profiles, written by Units.sync and read back at launch.
distanceUnit.off: Nothing, deliberately: kilometres or miles is how a screen reads rather than something a person stored, and a fresh install falls back to the locale. profiles.units is the truth and the launch task pulls it.

ancienttrees_session.why: The browser's own sign-in session. A session is what identifies the device; carrying it between devices is the one thing it must never do.

ancienttrees.last_fix.why: Where this phone last had a fix, so a cold start opens on your own trees rather than on Dam square. A property of the device, and stale on any other.

directions.app.why: Which maps app to hand a route to. Depends on what is installed on THIS phone, so copying it to another one would point at an app that is not there.

at_maps_app.why: The website's twin of directions.app (2026-09-24): which maps app an iPhone hands a route to. What is installed on this phone, so it stays on this phone.

at_contribute_draft.why: An unsent contribute form, kept so a reload does not lose what somebody typed. It stops existing the moment it is sent.

ancienttrees_pending.why: What somebody was doing at the moment they were asked to sign in, so the save survives the round trip through Google or an inbox and is finished when they land back (2026-09-18). The contribute draft's category exactly: an act begun and not finished rather than a thing a person has accumulated. At the moment it is written THERE IS NO ACCOUNT to hang it on, which is the whole situation it exists for; putting it on the server would mean identifying somebody who has not signed in.
ancienttrees_pending.off: Itself. Read and removed by SIGNIN_CATCH_JS the moment it is used, dropped when the sheet is dismissed without signing in, and ignored after half an hour.

at_notrack.why: This browser's opt-out of our own measurement (our button counts and Google Analytics). The convention everywhere is per-browser, and an account-wide copy would mean storing a preference against a person we deliberately do not profile.

hero.index.v1.why: Which hero picture was shown last, so the next launch shows a different one.

measure.install.v1.why: The analytics install id. It identifies an INSTALL on purpose and must not follow a person between devices.

measure.queue.v1.why: Events waiting for a network. Emptied as soon as they send.

nudge.fired.v1.why: Which nudges this phone has already used.

nudge.last.v1.why: When this phone last nudged, so it cannot nudge twice in a day.

reviewPrompt.fired.v2.why: Whether the App Store review prompt has fired here. Apple's own rule is per install.

reviewPrompt.last.v2.why: When it last fired on this install.

reviewPrompt.seen.v1.why: Which trees this install saw before asking.

reviewPrompt.yes.v1.why: The app version and day this install said yes to the review question, so it waits for a newer version.

at_id.why: A MapLibre feature property name, not persistence.

sb_publishable_qOTuw-LCejk2VhO2J6aXGQ_6X.why: Supabase's publishable key, which is a constant and not something we keep for anybody.

phc_nSwWiqWesJZmLMypTZDaeR3MDpcpBwcMpWRy.why: PostHog's project key, likewise a constant.

saved.saves_are_hearts_v1.why: The latch on the one-off saves-are-hearts repair of 2026-09-18 (CloudSync.repairSaves). Device rather than account on purpose: the repair identifies a stray row by asking THIS phone's own record of taps which entries are ticked-but-not-hearted, so a second device with a different local history has its own strays to clear. Syncing the latch would suppress a repair that device still needs. It is a bounded migration flag and carries no user data, so nothing is lost when the app is deleted.

saved.collected_leaves_want_v1.why: The latch on the one-off of 2026-10-19 (Saved.clearFulfilledWishes, run once from CloudSync.merge): hearts on trees this phone also holds as collected come off, here and in saves. Device for the same reason as saves_are_hearts_v1: each phone clears what its own copy still holds. A bounded migration flag, no user data.

file:CatalogueStore.swift.why: The last downloaded copy of OUR catalogue (trees, walks, species, browse) in Application Support, so the app opens offline. Nobody's data, the same on every phone, replaced on the next refresh.

at_consent.why: This browser's answer to the cookie bar (ConsentBar.astro, 2026-10-12). Consent to cookies is given per browser by law and by convention, and it is asked before anybody has signed in; an account-wide copy would carry a yes to a browser that was never asked.

plus.answered.v1.why: Whether this install answered the Ancient Trees Plus question, so its row on a city and in Settings goes away after the answer (Hidde, 2026-11-05: "ja dit mag je wel lokkaal opslaan", on "should the help create ancient trees plus thing go away once a user has answered it?"). Device by his word: the answer itself is anonymous (plus_answers has no account), so there is nothing on the server to hang it under, and like reviewPrompt.fired it is a question asked once per install. App: Screens/PlusAsk.swift.
plus.answered.v1.off: Nothing: a flag on this install, gone with the app; a new install asks again.

at_plus_answered.why: Whether this install answered the Ancient Trees Plus question, so its row on a city and in Settings goes away after the answer (Hidde, 2026-11-05: "ja dit mag je wel lokkaal opslaan", on "should the help create ancient trees plus thing go away once a user has answered it?"). Device by his word: the answer itself is anonymous (plus_answers has no account), so there is nothing on the server to hang it under, and like reviewPrompt.fired it is a question asked once per install. Website: components/PlusAsk.astro, localStorage.
at_plus_answered.off: Nothing: cleared with the browser's site data; a new browser asks again.

android:auth/session.refresh.why: The Android app's session (android/.../account/Account.kt), the refresh token only, in the app's private SharedPreferences with backup off. A session identifies the device and never travels; at launch it is spent with the server first and only the server's yes signs anybody in (hard rule 11).
android:auth/session.refresh.off: Sign out and account deletion remove it; the server revokes it on sign out.

android:device/plus.answered.v1.why: The Android twin of plus.answered.v1 (ui/PlaceBox.kt AppSwitches): whether this install answered the Ancient Trees Plus question, so its row on a city goes once answered (Hidde, 2026-11-05: "ja dit mag je wel lokkaal opslaan"). The answer itself is anonymous (plus_answers has no account), so there is nothing on the server to hang it under.
android:device/plus.answered.v1.off: Nothing: a flag on this install, gone with the app; a new install asks again.
